title: Two Materials. No Section.
format: 1280x720 / 24 fps / source photographs and plainly labeled scientific schematics
evidentiary_rule: No useful histological section was obtained. Do not depict hypothetical success or identifiable microscopic section results.

scenes.title: The section that never existed
scenes.subtitle: A FAILED HISTOLOGY ATTEMPT
scenes.narration: I wanted to see inside a developing zebrafish. These photographs are from an experiment that did not work.

scenes.title: Orientation mattered
scenes.subtitle: WHOLE LARVAE, NOT SECTIONS
scenes.narration: The specimens were tiny. A small change in orientation could decide whether a section passed through the anatomy I needed, or missed it entirely.

scenes.title: A temporary support
scenes.subtitle: 2% AGAROSE / CONCEPTUAL DIAGRAM
scenes.narration: My plan was to hold each specimen in a two percent agarose matrix. That support would establish orientation before subsequent tissue processing.

scenes.title: The paraffin stage
scenes.subtitle: EMBEDDING APPARATUS / ARCHIVE
scenes.narration: After dehydration and clearing, paraffin was meant to provide sufficient mechanical support for microtomy. On paper, each material had a reasonable job.

scenes.title: The material boundary
scenes.subtitle: SCHEMATIC / NOT EXPERIMENTAL MICROSCOPY
scenes.narration: But a hydrophilic gel and a hydrophobic embedding medium do not automatically form a mechanically coherent block. Their interface was the vulnerable point.

scenes.title: The block came apart
scenes.subtitle: OBSERVED FAILURE / ARCHIVAL PHOTO
scenes.narration: The processed block formed distinguishable layers. At the microtome, they separated and broke apart. A usable ribbon of histological sections never appeared.

scenes.title: What I could actually conclude
scenes.subtitle: OBSERVATION IS NOT MECHANISM
scenes.narration: The failure involved the materials, not simply the machine. But what I could observe was separation. Its precise physical explanation remained unresolved.

scenes.title: A hypothesis, not a diagnosis
scenes.subtitle: AGAROSE GRADE / NOT CONFIRMED
scenes.narration: The grade and thermal behaviour of agarose might have contributed. I did not establish that experimentally, and the photographs alone cannot prove it.

scenes.title: What a future test might ask
scenes.subtitle: PROPOSED CONTROLS / NOT PERFORMED
scenes.narration: A future comparison could examine agarose grade, concentration and processing conditions, then measure block integrity during sectioning. Those are proposals, not completed experiments.

scenes.title: No section. An intact record.
scenes.subtitle: FAILED ATTEMPT / FIRST-PERSON ACCOUNT
scenes.narration: No interpretable section came from this attempt. I kept the photographs anyway. The failed block was the evidence I had.
